verification_candidates.claim_text: Most magnesium supplements sold in shops either contain too low a dose of magnesium or are padded with filler ingredients.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: most of the stuff on the shelf either underdoses the magnesium or loads it with a bunch of filler i don't care about
verification_candidates.rationale: A checkable claim about the dosing and composition of magnesium supplements on the market that could change what a listener buys.

verification_candidates.claim_text: About half of the ingredients in multi-ingredient supplements are probably present at doses too small to have an effect.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: right and half of it is probably in there at doses too small to matter anyway
verification_candidates.rationale: A quantitative claim about supplement ingredient dosing that can be checked against product labels and dose-response evidence.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Dimming the lights and putting the phone away in the evening probably matters as much for winding down as taking the magnesium and L-theanine supplement.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: i pair it with dimming the lights and putting my phone away which probably matters just as much
verification_candidates.rationale: A comparative efficacy claim about sleep hygiene versus a supplement that could be checked against sleep research.
